title: API gateway and autoscaling
idea: An API gateway is the single entry point that routes each request to the right service. Autoscaling adds or removes copies of a service as load changes.
points: Clients call one address, and the gateway routes each path to its service.
It also runs shared checks, such as authentication and rate limits.
In Kubernetes, a pod is one running copy of a service.
The Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (HPA) adds pods above a CPU target, removes them below.

hero.title: One front door, a scaling service

steps.caption: Clients know one address: the API gateway. It checks the token, then picks a service by URL path.
A path of `/orders` goes to the orders service. A `/users` request would go to the users service.
Traffic grows. The single orders pod runs hot while the users service stays calm.
The HPA checks CPU use at a regular interval. Average use is above its target.
It raises the replica count, the number of pods wanted. Kubernetes starts two more pods.
The gateway now spreads `/orders` across three pods. Each pod carries less load.
Load falls. The HPA removes the extra pods again, but never goes below its minimum.

code.title: An HPA manifest
code.caption: Autoscale the `orders` Deployment between one and five pods. Step through it.

walk.text: `autoscaling/v2` is the API version; the kind is `HorizontalPodAutoscaler`.
`scaleTargetRef` names what to scale: the `orders` Deployment, which manages the pods.
Watch the CPU resource metric of the pods.
Aim for average CPU use at 70% of each pod's CPU request.

pitfalls: Give each container a CPU request; without it, a CPU utilization target is undefined.
Do not rely on the gateway alone for security; each service should still verify callers.
Autoscaling reacts after load rises, and new pods need time to start.

quiz.q: The HPA sees average CPU well above its target. What does it do?
options: Gives each pod more CPU and memory
Adds pods, up to the configured maximum
Routes requests to a different service
quiz.why: The HPA scales horizontally: it raises the replica count, within the minimum and maximum. Giving pods more CPU would be vertical scaling.

takeaway: The gateway is the front door; the HPA sets how many pods serve.
